frames.narration: One small server handles 80 requests per second. Its capacity is 100, so it is comfortable.
Traffic grows to 250 requests per second, far above the server's capacity. It slows down and starts failing requests.
Option A, scale up: replace it with a bigger machine. No code changes. 250 of 400 is fine.
The catch: one big machine is one point of failure, and there is a ceiling on how big it can get. If it dies, the whole site is down.
Option B, scale out: go back to small servers, add a load balancer, and run four of them.
The balancer shares the 250 requests per second. Each server handles about 62, well under its capacity of 100.
A server fails. The others absorb its share: 83 each, still under capacity. The site stays up.
More growth? Add a fifth server. The ceiling is the number of machines you can run, not the size of one.
